title: Retire the v1 vertical and legacy-plugin schema surface
summary: The platform wheel shipped thirty JSON schemas that no authored code and no live test reached: the v1 vertical audit ledger family (audit-ledger plus its referenced children and the page, object, operation, evidence, finding, decision, and registry schemas), the v1 observability and public-progress contracts (runtime-event, observability-manifest, performance-bill, public-progress), and the legacy executable-plugin conformance family (plugin-conformance, plugin-fixture, plugin-release, plugin-release-acceptance) left behind when the Python plugin conformance chain was deleted. Scope: schemas/ held 45 files; exactly 15 are named by a live loader under src/, packages/*/src, plugins/*/src, or scripts/ (canonical-result, capability-negotiation, compiled-plugin-contract, design-confirmation, lifecycle-acceptance, parallel-execution, platform-ledger, platform-performance-bill, plugin-lifecycle-plan, plugin-lifecycle-transaction, private-runtime-cleanup, provider-conformance, provider-execution, provider-fixture, provider-release). The other 30 had no reader: they were reachable only from schemas/README.md, from each other, or from the retired v1 test. No kept schema references a deleted one, and no deleted schema is referenced by any authored code, so removing them cannot change runtime behaviour. This change deletes the 30 schemas, replaces the v1-only test with tests/test_schema_contracts.py (which keeps the two live schema acceptance cases) and removes tests/test_observability_schema.py, rewrites schemas/README.md to the live inventory with a historical note for the retired surface, and extends scripts/check_architecture_boundaries.py so every schema in schemas/ must be reachable from an authored literal or a $ref chain unless it is registered as an explicit author-facing contract, a retired schema name cannot return even if a reader is added, and schemas/README.md cannot reintroduce retired protocol tool vocabulary. Classification is breaking because the assayer-platform wheel stops shipping these thirty files; no live loader, compiled contract, ledger, result schema, plugin, provider, or Host behaviour changes. Verification evidence: the change landed in LANDING_COMMIT, pushed on 2026-09-17, and CI run CI_RUN passed all seven jobs; locally the architecture check returns 0 on the repository, its thirteen tests pass including an orphan schema that is rejected and a retired schema name that is rejected even with a reader, the design confirmation gate returns 0 across the changed range, and the fast and full profiles, the document, plugin-source, English text, and resilience gates all stay green.

platform: Platform governance owns the platform schema resource directory, the architecture gate, and the schema inventory
plugin: No plugin change; ordinary plugins compile to compiled-plugin.json and never loaded the removed schemas
provider: No provider change; provider packages use provider-release, provider-fixture, provider-execution, provider-conformance, and capability-negotiation, which stay in place
agent: No agent change; the removed schemas had no live reader and the retired agent distribution is already gone

forbiddenResponsibilities: The change must not alter any live schema, compiled contract, platform ledger, or result contract, or any live Host, plugin, provider, or SDK behaviour
The change must not remove the live platform and SDK schemas that the compiled acceptance and conformance paths validate
The change must not reintroduce a retired v1 or legacy-plugin schema, or ship a platform schema with no live reader, without an explicit author-facing registration
The gate must not reject the live schemas, the SDK-owned schemas, or a schema that is reachable only through a cross-file $ref
acceptance: schemas/ contains only the fifteen schemas that a live loader names, and none of the thirty retired schema names exist
tests/test_observability_schema.py does not exist and tests/test_schema_contracts.py keeps the live platform-ledger and plugin-manifest acceptance cases

scripts/check_architecture_boundaries.py rejects a schema in schemas/ with no live reader, rejects a retired schema name even when a reader is added, and rejects retired protocol tool vocabulary in schemas/README.md
no kept schema references a deleted schema and the schema store loads without the removed files

the architecture, document, plugin-source, English text, and resilience gates stay green, the design confirmation gate is green across the changed range, and the fast, full, and compiled acceptance profiles still pass

humanApproval.decision: Release-surface change carried out under the standing authorization of the refactor mandate in #assayer-group:4c84ee19 and its delegation update, under which the agent and reviewer decide these changes themselves within at most seven workflow rounds. The classification is breaking because the assayer-platform wheel stops shipping thirty unreachable schemas; the evidence that nothing in the repository consumed them is recorded in the summary. @assayer_rev independently requested this round and reviews the batch; a published-surface removal is classified as a release change by established precedent.
